about.headline: The person behind the work.
about.body:
I'm Wafa Alhayek, an artist, writer and data practitioner working in Nablus. My practice moves between analogue and digital, intuition and analysis, image and text.

The images are untitled and will stay that way. Titles ask a work to explain itself, and these don't. What the index gives instead is an address: the capture number assigned when the file was made, kept in sequence.

Much of the source material comes from the British Library's Flickr Commons release: over a million public-domain images from digitised 17th, 18th and 19th century books.

game.headline: Draw a plate.
game.intro: Three works, face down. Choose one.
lines: Some things become smaller when named too quickly.
An image can hold a contradiction without resolving it.
The number is an address, not an interpretation.
Every fragment was once part of something whole.
Look again. It was there the first time.
